correctness.rationale: The inversion-graph components equal 1 plus the number of proper direct-sum cuts J_k. Conditioned on J_k, left and right position blocks are independently uniform permutations of their respective value intervals. Cross-block pattern probability is 1_{j in D(tau)}/(j!(m-j)!) instead of 1/m!, and weighting by Pr(J_k)=1/binom(n,k) proves the universal finite sum. For 2143 only j=2 is a cut, giving (-1,5,-1)/24 coefficients. Independent brute force of uniform permutations n=4..7 and exact rational evaluation of n=4..39 verified the coefficients and sign. For n>=40 the proof preserves negative endpoint terms giving -D_n and bounds interior positive B_k by binomial estimates; D_n>=n²/100 dominates 5n/48 for n>=40, so all n proved. Finite enumeration alone is not used to infer the infinite sign.

evidence: Acan–Pittel analyze K conditional on inversion count, not X_tau conditional on J_k; Janson et al. enumerate mixed pattern counts.

value.rationale: The statistic couples global inversion-graph block structure with local pattern counts and reveals a surprising all-size sign reversal at a sharp finite boundary. The universal dependency only on a pattern direct-sum fingerprint is a nontrivial structural classification relevant to random permutation statistics.

final_claim: For a uniform permutation Pi_n, the covariance of its inversion-graph component count K_n and any ordinary pattern-count X_tau (n>=m>=2) is the explicit two-level binomial sum depending only on the proper direct-sum cut set D(tau). For tau=2143=21+21, covariance is strictly positive at n=4..7 and strictly negative at every n>=8.
